confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on three web searches of aggregated price sources: citycost.org (inexpensive meal about $10.02, mid-range three-course meal for two about $45.70, cappuccino about $5.82), numbeo.com (inexpensive meal $10, mid-range meal for two $45, mid-range bottle of wine $20) and 2026 budget guides (gotripzi.com and machupicchu.org; local Zambezi lager about $4.95-4.98, cold beer from $3, cocktails about $8-12, and $8-15 at hotel bars). Sources disagree. Cappuccino estimates range from about $2 to $6, so I used a midpoint suited to a tourist town. No aggregated source gave a reliable draft beer price, so the beer figure is bounded between local bars (about $1-3) and hotel bars ($4-8). No source gave a typical price for a glass of wine, so wine_glass is inferred from the roughly $20 bottle price and the local beer-to-wine price relationship. One search result was a menu from Disney's Victoria Falls Lounge in Florida, not this city, and I ignored it. Food prices were nudged up slightly for the July 2026 peak dry season. Accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge only, without any live listings checked. Victoria Falls is a tourist town priced in USD, with few true hostels and expensive mid-range hotels in peak season, so the hostel and hotel anchors are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: I treated Victoria Falls as a small, USD-priced safari and adventure tourism hub, comparable to Livingstone (Zambia) and Kasane (Botswana). Its restaurant and drink prices sit well above Bulawayo or Harare local rates, and peak-season accommodation is priced more like a premium Southern African tourist destination than a typical Zimbabwean town.
